clue.text: Covering roots of the deciduous, elm tree soil -

indicators.note: the tree is wrapped round the other letters, covering them like a canopy

parts.note: the birch is a common deciduous tree

indicators.note: a word's roots here are its final letters, the bottom end of each of the three words

explanation.surface: A gardener describes a ground cover of leaf litter and soil beneath deciduous elms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Covering' puts BIRCH round E, S and M, the last letters of 'the deciduous elm'. 'soil' is the verb, to dirty.
explanation.definitionFit: To soil something is to dirty or sully it, and the word is used of reputations too.

clue.text: Some suspicion about diamonds' size

indicators.note: the suspicion word surrounds the diamonds letter

parts.note: a breath of scandal is a hint or slight suspicion
D is the card-game abbreviation for diamonds

explanation.surface: A jeweller is somewhat suspicious about how big the diamonds are.
explanation.definitionFit: Breadth is width, one measure of how large something is.

clue.text: The musical for Cleopatra's youth

definitions.meaning: a 1954 British stage musical by Julian Slade
Shakespeare's Cleopatra calls her youth the time when she was green in judgment

explanation.surface: A show tune written about the young Egyptian queen.
explanation.walkthrough: In Antony and Cleopatra the queen speaks of her younger years with this phrase, which also titles a long-running London musical.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a time of youthful inexperience, coined by Shakespeare's Cleopatra, and is also a famous British show.

clue.text: And I set off as a stand-in

indicators.note: set off suggests the letters being sent off in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone sets out on a journey as a replacement for another person.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something in place of another, as a substitute or alternative would.

clue.text: Solid oil in motor -: speed zero

indicators.note: the speed and zero letters are placed inside the motor

parts.note: a motor is a car
mph, miles per hour, measures speed
O looks like the figure zero

explanation.surface: A mechanic notes solid oil in the engine and the speedometer reading nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Camphor is a waxy solid essential oil from the camphor tree.

clue.text: Man to boil a tongue

parts.note: a man is referred to as he
to brew is to boil or steep, as with tea or beer

explanation.surface: Someone tells a man to bring water to the boil for tea, or perhaps to cook an ox tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: A tongue is a language, and this is the language of Israel and of Jewish scripture.

clue.text: A tricky problem, making stew with only half a tomato

parts.note: a hotpot is a meat and potato stew, as in Lancashire hotpot

indicators.note: only the back half of the word tomato is kept

explanation.surface: A cook faces a dilemma making a stew with just part of a tomato.
explanation.walkthrough: 'only half a' keeps ATO, the second half of TOMATO. Lancashire hotpot is a traditional English lamb stew.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot potato is an awkward issue nobody wants to handle, an idiom for a delicate question.

clue.text: A brilliant performance you… 'are heard in, well done, Madam!

indicators.note: the heard letters go inside the cry of praise

parts.note: brava is the cry of applause for a woman performer

indicators.note: the two words are spoken and sound like two letters

parts.note: said aloud, you are sounds like the letters U and R

explanation.surface: An audience member praises a female singer's performance.
explanation.definitionFit: Bravura is great technical skill and brilliance shown in a performance.

clue.text: Put on a jury, see me upset over the accused in Scotland

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits over, above, the second
in a down clue the word is turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: taken as written before turning
in Scots law the defendant is called the panel

explanation.surface: A Scottish juror is distressed to see the defendant in court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'see' is a link. In Scots law the accused person is termed 'the panel'.
explanation.definitionFit: To empanel is to enrol or choose people to serve as jurors.

clue.text: Not a sentimental motive for becoming a soldier

indicators.note: read as moving or in motion, it tells us the letters of the word before it are shifted around

parts.note: the fodder word, used once the a is removed

explanation.surface: Someone joins the army for hard practical reasons, not out of any romantic feeling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not a' removes one A from SENTIMENTAL, and 'motive' shuffles the remaining ten letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Enlisting is signing up for military service, so the noun is the act of joining the forces.

clue.text: A record's high up in Europe

parts.note: an LP is a long-playing record, so record's gives LP plus S

explanation.surface: A recording reaches the top of the European charts.
explanation.definitionFit: This mountain range stands high above central Europe, from France to Austria.

clue.text: To avoid work, has Dutch model gone out?

indicators.note: gone out of order, the letters are scattered and reassembled

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a Dutch fashion model has stepped out of the shop to dodge her shift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' acts on DUTCH MODEL GONE, all fourteen letters rearranged. To dodge the column is old British military slang for shirking duty.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is British slang, from soldiers keeping out of the marching column, for shirking a job.

clue.text: Grey-haired, the German treasurer

parts.note: hoar means grey or white with age, as in hoary
der is the German masculine word for the

explanation.surface: A grey-haired German official is in charge of the money.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who treasures and stockpiles valuables, keeping them close, treasures them as a miser does.

clue.text: Out of sulphur, say? I've more, than enough

indicators.note: signals that the letters are spoken aloud to give a different word

parts.note: ex means out of, and S is the chemical symbol for sulphur
taken as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: A chemist asks if they have run out of sulphur, then admits to having a surplus.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken quickly, 'ex' followed by the letter name 'ess' runs together into one familiar word for surplus.
explanation.definitionFit: Excessive means going beyond what is needed or reasonable.

clue.text: Emperor's taking southern region in french city

parts.note: Caen is a city in Normandy
an area is a region

explanation.surface: A Roman emperor seizes a southern area within a city in France.
explanation.definitionFit: Caesarean means relating to Caesar, the title of the Roman emperors.

clue.text: Fool in bird's clothing

indicators.note: the fool goes inside the bird

parts.note: a cock is a male bird, especially a rooster
an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: A clown is dressed up in a bird costume.
explanation.definitionFit: A long garment worn by clergy and choristers, so a piece of clerical clothing.

clue.text: To shock us and to stagger

indicators.note: staggering means reeling about, so the letters lurch into a new order

explanation.surface: Something startles us and makes us reel.
explanation.definitionFit: To astound is to amaze or stun someone greatly.

clue.text: One of the marks Sherlock Holmes's band was entitled to

definitions.text: One of the marks Sherlock Holmes's band was entitled to

parts.words: One of the marks Sherlock Holmes's band was entitled to
parts.note: a small spot or mark, the singular of the marks that give the title of the Conan Doyle story The Adventure of the ... Band

explanation.surface: A question about which marks belong to a band of musicians led by Sherlock Holmes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entitled' means named in a title: the Conan Doyle story is The Speckled Band.
explanation.definitionFit: A small spot or fleck of colour; the band in the Holmes story was covered in such spots.

clue.text: Hair-dresser's rollers

definitions.meaning: read as hairdressers, people who comb and groom hair
long curling waves that roll in and break on a beach

explanation.surface: Curlers used in a hairdressing salon.
explanation.walkthrough: The rollers are not curlers but breaking waves; the possessive reads as a plural of people who comb hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Long rolling waves that curl over and break are called by this name, as are people who groom hair.

clue.text: Bird conceals her smoke

indicators.note: the bird wraps round and hides the other word

parts.note: a coot is a black waterbird

explanation.surface: A bird hides a woman's cigarette.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheroot is a cigar with both ends cut square, something to smoke.

clue.text: The wrong documents I am looking up

indicators.note: in a down clue, looking up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: deeds are legal documents
I'm is the contraction of I am

explanation.surface: Someone checks the papers and finds a mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: A misdeed is a wrongful act, the wrong done.

clue.text: Used a test to discover drugs

indicators.note: to discover is to uncover something tucked inside the words

explanation.surface: A test was used to detect drugs in an athlete.
explanation.definitionFit: To sedate someone is to calm them with a drug, so drugs is the verb.

clue.text: Natural desires run wild in this book

indicators.note: the letters are let loose and rearranged

explanation.surface: A novel in which human instincts are given free rein.
explanation.walkthrough: 'run wild' rearranges NATURAL DESIRES; the result is Robert Louis Stevenson's pirate novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Stevenson's adventure story of pirates and buried gold is a famous book.

clue.text: Stuff poultry

definitions.meaning: a strong cotton or linen cloth, stuff meaning fabric
a domestic waterfowl kept for eggs and meat

explanation.definitionFit: Stuff is an old word for fabric, and this heavy canvas is one; the farmyard waterfowl is poultry.

clue.text: Unable to talk clearly about business, that's natural

indicators.note: the natural word is placed around the business abbreviation

parts.note: inherent means natural or built-in
Co is the abbreviation for company, a business

explanation.surface: Someone cannot speak sensibly about work, which is only to be expected.
explanation.definitionFit: Incoherent speech is muddled and hard to follow, so the speaker cannot express things plainly.

clue.text: Stick a poster in this site

parts.note: a poster is an advertisement, an ad
this site is here, the place where we are

explanation.surface: An instruction to put up a bill on this spot.
explanation.definitionFit: To adhere is to cling or remain fixed, as glue does.

clue.text: They are learning from French dwarfs outside

indicators.note: the dwarfing word goes around the French word

parts.note: stunts means checks the growth of, dwarfs
de is French for from

explanation.surface: Pupils study the dwarfs of French folklore.
explanation.definitionFit: Students are people who study, pupils engaged in learning.
